contests.districtNotes: District 8 covers all of Brunswick County, all of Columbus County, and a portion of New Hanover County (including downtown Wilmington). The New Hanover portion was added after 2020 redistricting and has been criticized as a partisan gerrymander. Rabon has held this seat since 2011 and has never lost. His 2024 margin was approximately +20 points.
contests.primaryOutcome: All three party primaries (Republican, Democratic, Libertarian) were canceled. Each candidate advanced to the general election without appearing on the primary ballot. No primary contest occurred.

candidates.termHistory: Won elections in 2010, 2012, 2014, 2016, 2018, 2020, 2022, and 2024. Running for a 9th term in 2026.
candidates.professionalBackground: Veterinarian and small businessman. Doctor of Veterinary Medicine (University of Georgia, 1976). Partner in multiple animal hospitals in Brunswick County. Operates family farm in Winnabow, NC. Vice Chair, Brunswick Community College Board of Trustees.
education: Doctor of Veterinary Medicine, University of Georgia (1976)
candidates.notableBackground: Eagle Scout. Received the American Farmer Degree (highest FFA honor) upon high school graduation in 1969.
candidates.legislativeRole: Chairman, Rules and Operations of the Senate (2025-2026 session). Chairman, Select Committee on Nominations. Previously chaired Appropriations on Department of Transportation. One of the most senior and powerful members of the North Carolina Senate Republican caucus.
candidates.notes: Long-serving incumbent with a full voting record available via NC General Assembly website and VoteSmart. Rules Committee chairmanship makes him one of the most powerful figures in the NC Senate. No known announced retirement. District drawn to strongly favor Republicans. Previous Democratic challenger (Katherine Randall, 2024) received approximately 40% despite campaign effort.

ballotMeasures.officialTitle: North Carolina Require Voter Identification Amendment
ballotMeasures.shortName: Voter ID for All Voters Amendment
ballotMeasures.yesVoteMeans: Amends the North Carolina Constitution to require photographic identification for ALL voters, including those voting by absentee/mail-in ballot. Current law only requires photo ID for in-person voters.
ballotMeasures.noVoteMeans: Maintains the status quo: photo ID required for in-person voters only. Mail-in/absentee voters continue to be exempt from the photo ID requirement.

legislativePassage.house: Passed 73-45 on December 11, 2024 (73 Republicans, 1 Democrat in favor)

ballotMeasures.context: North Carolina voters approved a constitutional photo voter ID requirement for in-person voting in 2018 (55.49% yes). This measure extends that requirement to absentee/mail-in voters. It must again be approved by voters as a constitutional amendment.
ballotMeasures.proponentArgument: Voter ID is a commonsense security measure that should apply equally to all voters regardless of voting method (Senator Warren Daniel, sponsor).
ballotMeasures.opponentArgument: Another attempt to disenfranchise voters by mail; will create barriers for elderly, disabled, and rural voters (Democracy North Carolina).
